claims.text: The applicable alloy composition is equimolar CoCrFeNiTi, corresponding nominally to 20 at.% of each element.
The initial alloy is in a simple solid-solution state.
The equimolar CoCrFeNiTi alloy has low hardness and strength.
The alloy lacks significant lattice distortion.
Its simple solid-solution state and lack of significant lattice distortion or precipitates make dislocation glide and slip-system activation easy.
Easy dislocation glide and slip-system activation govern the alloy's low hardness and strength.
Easy dislocation glide and slip-system activation lead to extensive plastic deformation.
At room temperature and a strain rate of 10^-3 s^-1, the alloy will have a yield strength of approximately 400 MPa.
At room temperature and a strain rate of 10^-3 s^-1, the alloy will reach approximately 50% elongation at fracture.
In-situ neutron diffraction and EBSD will reveal significant dislocation activity during deformation.
In-situ neutron diffraction and EBSD will reveal significant slip-system activation during deformation.
The proposed loading directions are <100> and <111>.
The proposed mechanism is bounded to equimolar CoCrFeNiTi in a simple solid-solution state.

contradictions.description: Room temperature is presented as an applicability boundary while the same fields also call for varying temperature, leaving the actual temperature boundary ambiguous.
